instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Hope Keeps Moving
cards.instruction: Turn every disappointment into a new reason the desired outcome is delayed, redirected, or becoming more meaningful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall rejected our wedding booking. Cross it off neatly, please. A refusal tells us which venue wasn't right for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every venue is booked for June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then turn to September. Not August; we need time to plan properly. Three extra months will make the wedding worth waiting for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My parents can't travel in September.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we go to them. Put 'their garden' on the list, please, and ring your mum before you confirm anything. We needed somewhere she'd actually be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our bookshop failed here. Please label these boxes by subject, not 'leftovers'. We're taking the books to the right readers next time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have no moving money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one box to start. Choose deliberately, please; this is how we learn what people actually want rather than renting another empty room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can get us a market stall beside the bus stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short stories, then. Not the collected works; they need something before their bus arrives. Pack that box. We've finally found people with a reason to stop.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Comfort Everyone Else
cards.instruction: Meet every painful moment by comforting someone else more intensely while your own distress becomes harder to hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We were both laid off, but you need a proper cup of tea. Sit down, please. I'll get the tissues open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're wiping your eyes on your sleeve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These soft ones are for you. Feet on the floor, please; curling up won't help. Tell me what you're worried about.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You. Your hands are shaking so much you can't open the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then hold it steady while I pull. Not that end, the perforation. We'll get you a tissue. Please keep holding it; I can't quite make my fingers work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made soup. Being rejected by the choir doesn't mean you skip dinner. Small spoonfuls first, please; it's hot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't touched yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm making sure you're settled. Bread with the butter side up, please. I'll fetch you another piece.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit down. I can hear you crying whenever you go into the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Bring the bread here. I'll hold your plate. Butter right to the corners, please; I can't see them clearly enough to do it for you.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Emotional Interest
cards.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told your mother I'm afraid she dislikes me. At Sunday lunch, I need an equally risky admission from you. Think about it properly, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to tell her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That doesn't make the risk disappear. Please compare what we each exposed, not who requested it. What are you afraid she'll think?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That you're the child she wishes she'd had.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the right level. Now tell her, not just me. Same lunch table, same audience. Please don't count a rehearsal as repayment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sit with you while you tell your brother you lost the deposit. Next time, you sit through an equally difficult admission from me. Say yes before we ring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're charging me for being frightened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not for fear. For staying while someone hears the truth. Please keep those separate. I need to know you'll take that risk with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know if I could. I'd want to make an excuse and leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say 'I might leave', please. 'I don't know' conceals the risk. I'll count the plain version as a first payment; you still owe me the staying.

cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about last night's rent argument. Start there, please, not with a summary of everything I've done this year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters. You've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It does. But that's a conclusion. Ask one question, and let me finish the answer before you explain it back to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Please don't turn that into a departure date; let the fact sit here for a minute.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about trying again, but I'll sit beside the door. Please move that chair; an exit needs to stay clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you planning to run?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're confusing an available exit with a plan to use it. Knowing I can leave is what lets me sit down. Shall we begin?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop whenever you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I want to come home. Please treat that as a statement, not a moving arrangement. Ask me how it feels before you offer a key.

cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: The Same Ending
cards.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your message ends 'take care'. Please don't call that casual. It was the first phrase in my last breakup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You have a cold. I meant get better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how it starts: they get you healthy enough to leave. Please read the sequence, not just this one message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring you soup tonight. I want to look after you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the final kindness. Bring it in your own saucepan, please, not a tub you can abandon. We should at least be precise about what you're returning for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've cancelled lunch. Please don't tell me it's just one meal; that's how the key comes back a month later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm exhausted. I haven't said anything about keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. You're mixing stages. First I'm tiring, then my calls are tiring, then you need your space. I've been through this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow, then. I'll book our usual table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A public place. Yes, that's the next stage. Book the corner, please; if you're going to leave me, I'd rather not have to stand up in the middle of the room.
